title: How Punch and others sat while playing
summary: Punch describes sitting with legs crossed after his operation, stomping his foot, and Ed Marsh playing his horn sideways.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: How do you sit when you play ordinarily?
Well, most of my time, I sit in this position.
Mm-hmm.
But I got the earring with this thing where I got operated on. I sit like this all the time. Looked like that just to help me, you know.
With your legs crossed.
Yeah.
That helps you, huh?
Mm-hmm. Helped me.
Before you, since you had your operation.
Since I had my operation?
Since you had your operation, you sit with your legs crossed, huh?

Oh, no. Before that, I said when I started the earring with that pain there. Yeah. I used to cross my leg. That's before the operation. But before I had that, I used to sit all the time straight like that.
Just straight up and down with it. And your legs spread apart a little.
Yeah. Because I used to stomp this foot, you know, all the time.
Your right foot, you stomp the heel, huh?
Yeah.
Did many guys sit funny when they played? Or wiggle around?
Well, Ed Marsh used to sit crossways for some old reason. He never did play this way with the band. He always played his horn this way.
Out to the side, huh?
Yeah, out on the side. The band be playing this way, he be playing over there. I used to get at him about that all the time.
I guess the people didn't like that.
Huh?
People didn't like that, huh?
No, no.
Well, Raymond Burke sure does wiggle now.
Yeah.
